subject.title: Crons ejecutaron mensajes de WhatsApp a la 1 AM fuera de horario y no se podían detener

question: Should this issue be resolved by splitting the restart replay fix from a separate emergency-stop/delete semantics decision, or should one change expand cron remove/gateway stop to abort live outbound delivery now?
rationale: Current source proves the replay bug is still present, but the user’s full request also needs a product boundary for operator cancellation across cron, task registry, gateway lifecycle, and WhatsApp delivery.

options.title: Split Replay Fix And Stop Semantics
options.body: Review and land or replace the schedule-activation PR for restart replay first, then design the emergency outbound stop/delete contract as a follow-up.

options.title: Expand One Fix Across Runtime Stop Paths
options.body: Require one broader implementation that changes cron remove and gateway stop to abort live outbound cron delivery, accepting the larger compatibility and ownership surface.

options.title: Limit Scope To Restart Replay
options.body: Treat the emergency-stop request as separate product work and close this only after the replay subset lands with a clearly linked follow-up.

recommendation.title: Split Replay Fix And Stop Semantics
recommendation.body: Review and land or replace the schedule-activation PR for restart replay first, then design the emergency outbound stop/delete contract as a follow-up.

likelyOwner.reason: Recent cron timer history plus maintainer verification on the related activation-boundary PR make this the best available owner for the product-boundary decision.
